sources.title: Relevé de couverture anthroponymique EthniAfrica
sources.notes: This name appears in our coverage list: it has been selected as a name to document, but no dedicated source has yet been consulted. The fiche therefore exists to flag the name, not for what it states about it. Forthcoming checks will draw on electoral registers, national statistical institutes and the onomastic scholarship of the country concerned.

sources.title: Bamadaba — dictionnaire des noms claniques (jamuw)
sources.notes: Onomastic annex of the Bamadaba, the Bambara-French electronic dictionary supplementing the Corpus bambara de référence (Bailleul, Davydov, Erman, Maslinsky, Méric, Vydrin, 2011-2020, CC BY-NC-SA); the clan-name annex is identified as such by Vydrin, « Vers une lexicographie mandingue sur la base de grands corpus annotés », Mandenkan 63, 2020, pp. 89-110. The entry Bagayogo, a spelling close to the Bagayoko used here, carries a joking-partner marker (senankun) toward Sangaré; links of this kind are not systematically reciprocal from one entry to another, but this one is carried by the Bagayogo entry itself.

sources.title: Pouvoir, places et filiation : les senankuya au Mali
sources.notes: Canut, Cécile, Cahiers de praxématique, number 38, 2002, pp. 175-197. Fieldwork in Mali. She states what the pact requires: the relationship holds in perpetuity for the whole descent of both lineages, marriage between them is forbidden — variably applied today, she notes — and mutual aid is owed without reserve. Cited for the obligation itself; it does not name the pair in this entry, which is carried by the entries cited alongside it.

sources.title: Pactes, alliances et plaisanteries. Pratiques locales, discours global
sources.notes: Canut, Cécile, and Smith, Étienne, Cahiers d'études africaines, number 184, 2006, p. 687 and following. Cited for the caution it raises: the idea that joking kinship pacifies conflict is treated there as a hypothesis inherited from Radcliffe-Brown and taken up by conflict-resolution studies, hence as a discourse to be analysed rather than as a measured effect. The starting page is verified; the closing page is not.

sources.title: Bakayoko — origine, signification et incidence du nom de famille
sources.notes: Worldwide genealogical aggregator, consulted on 29 September 2026. Worldwide incidence of about 101,645 bearers; Côte d'Ivoire 95,088, Mali 2,517, Guinea 1,912, France 814, Burkina Faso 317. The page gives no meaning for the name. The figures outside Africa are not carried into the attestations of this fiche. Bakayoko is the most widely borne spelling; the dictionary of jamuw gives Bagayoko and Bagayogo for the same entry.
